speaker: gauge
text: Iron can't burn. So iron buildings are fireproof, right?

speaker: fitz
text:
People thought so, until Chicago's 1871 fire.
Iron doesn't burn. But heat makes it weak, and hot columns can bend and give way. "Fireproof" buildings were destroyed too.

speaker: gauge
text: So how do you stop the heat?

speaker: fitz
text: Wrap the iron. Builders started covering it in terra cotta tile, a kind of fired clay, to keep it cooler.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
